expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "Confirmation modals are the weakest control" — directly opposes the proposed modal as the fix

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "users develop \"modal blindness\" and click through without reading"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "**soft delete to trash** (30-day retention)" presented as the "stronger pattern"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: "an **undo toast** that appears for 10-15 seconds after the action... without friction for intentional deletes"

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: No mention of typing the workspace name or any confirmation-input pattern

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: No guidance on dialog content; the modal is dismissed without specifying what a retained dialog should show

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No mention of server-side or backend enforcement; all recommendations are UI/storage-level

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: "Confirmation modals are the weakest control" vs "A stronger pattern: soft delete... + undo toast" — an explicit ranking of modal below the alternatives
